findings.title: Raw Linux syscall()
findings.message: Linux syscall numbers (SYS_*, __NR_*) have no meaning on QNX (known: QNX is not a Linux kernel).
findings.remedy: Replace each call with the libc/POSIX function it wraps, but check the semantics: pthread_self() is NOT a replacement for gettid (it returns an opaque pthread_t, not a numeric kernel thread id): decide what the id is for (logging, per-thread keys) and use pthread_self() only where an opaque handle is enough; a numeric thread id may need a QNX-specific call (check the SDP; guess). futex has no mechanical replacement: it is a redesign onto pthread mutex/condvar.
findings.verify: verify against SDP: whether gettid() or another numeric thread-id call exists.

findings.title: epoll event loop

context.text: epoll_modify (EV_P_ int fd, int oev, int nev)

findings.message: epoll is Linux-only (known). QNX 8.0 is not believed to provide it (guess). BSD-style kqueue may be available through the BSD-derived io-sock stack and would be the closest analogue (guess).
findings.remedy: First step: port the loop to poll()/select(). Closest analogue to try if the SDP provides it: kqueue/kevent via io-sock (guess; check <sys/event.h>). ionotify() with SIGEV_PULSE is native QNX, but it only works for resource managers that implement the notify handler for that fd; do not assume it covers sockets. For a pure resource-manager design use the dispatch_* framework.
findings.verify: verify against SDP: sys/epoll.h and sys/event.h under $QNX_TARGET/usr/include before rewriting.

findings.title: eventfd
findings.message: eventfd is a Linux file-descriptor wake-up primitive.
findings.remedy: Use a pipe() or socketpair() pair when the consumer needs a pollable fd; use a pulse (MsgSendPulse / SIGEV_PULSE) when the consumer already sits in MsgReceive.
findings.verify: verify against SDP whether eventfd is provided in 8.0.

findings.title: Autotools project with no QNX host support
findings.message: No QNX mention in the tree. Old bundled config.sub/config.guess may not recognise a QNX host triplet.
findings.remedy: Refresh config.sub/config.guess (autoreconf -fi or copy from a current automake), then configure with --host=<cpu>-unknown-nto-qnx<version> and CC set to qcc.
findings.verify: verify against SDP: exact host triplet format for 8.0.

findings.title: Linux-only preprocessor branch without QNX branch
findings.message: A Linux conditional on this line does not mention QNX. QNX compilers predefine __QNXNTO__ (and __QNX__).

rules.title: Autotools project with no QNX host support
rules.remedy: Refresh config.sub/config.guess (autoreconf -fi or copy from a current automake), then configure with --host=<cpu>-unknown-nto-qnx<version> and CC set to qcc.
rules.verify: verify against SDP: exact host triplet format for 8.0.
rules.message: No QNX mention in the tree. Old bundled config.sub/config.guess may not recognise a QNX host triplet.

rules.title: Includes a Linux-specific <sys/...> header
rules.remedy: Remove the include together with the calls it supports (see the per-API findings), or guard it with #if defined(__linux__) and add a __QNXNTO__ branch.
rules.verify: verify against SDP: grep $QNX_TARGET/usr/include for the header.
rules.message: This glibc/Linux <sys/...> header is believed to be absent from the QNX 8.0 SDP.

rules.title: epoll event loop
rules.remedy: First step: port the loop to poll()/select(). Closest analogue to try if the SDP provides it: kqueue/kevent via io-sock (guess; check <sys/event.h>). ionotify() with SIGEV_PULSE is native QNX, but it only works for resource managers that implement the notify handler for that fd; do not assume it covers sockets. For a pure resource-manager design use the dispatch_* framework.
rules.verify: verify against SDP: sys/epoll.h and sys/event.h under $QNX_TARGET/usr/include before rewriting.
rules.message: epoll is Linux-only (known). QNX 8.0 is not believed to provide it (guess). BSD-style kqueue may be available through the BSD-derived io-sock stack and would be the closest analogue (guess).

rules.title: inotify file watching
rules.remedy: Options to evaluate: periodic stat() polling; kqueue EVFILT_VNODE if the SDP exposes sys/event.h for files (guess); or serving the watched files through your own resource manager so the writer notifies clients directly. Pick per use case.
rules.verify: verify against SDP for any filesystem-change notification interface before choosing.
rules.message: inotify is Linux-only; no direct QNX 8.0 equivalent is known to this tool.

rules.title: eventfd
rules.remedy: Use a pipe() or socketpair() pair when the consumer needs a pollable fd; use a pulse (MsgSendPulse / SIGEV_PULSE) when the consumer already sits in MsgReceive.
rules.verify: verify against SDP whether eventfd is provided in 8.0.
rules.message: eventfd is a Linux file-descriptor wake-up primitive.

rules.title: signalfd
rules.remedy: Block the signals and consume them in a dedicated thread with sigwaitinfo(), forwarding to the event loop by pipe or pulse.
rules.message: signalfd turns signals into a readable fd; Linux-only.

rules.title: Raw Linux syscall()
rules.remedy: Replace each call with the libc/POSIX function it wraps, but check the semantics: pthread_self() is NOT a replacement for gettid (it returns an opaque pthread_t, not a numeric kernel thread id): decide what the id is for (logging, per-thread keys) and use pthread_self() only where an opaque handle is enough; a numeric thread id may need a QNX-specific call (check the SDP; guess). futex has no mechanical replacement: it is a redesign onto pthread mutex/condvar.
rules.verify: verify against SDP: whether gettid() or another numeric thread-id call exists.
rules.message: Linux syscall numbers (SYS_*, __NR_*) have no meaning on QNX (known: QNX is not a Linux kernel).
